This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place, no matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herst. The Democrat in Alaska's tight Senate race, Mary Peltola, is among those asking a judge to toss a Justice Department's lawsuit that President Trump personally ordered, trying to block certification of results if incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan loses because of another candidate with the same name.
But Attorney General Todd Blanche is defending his agency's move.
Why is this controversial? The fact that I'm saying that voters, that they are so confused by what a candidate has done in literally making up a candidacy to try to confuse voters, that we're going to try to create a situation where that can be remedied.
That shouldn't be something that is causing this shock and horror. That should be what every single Alaskan expects of their government.
Speaking there on CNN's State of the Union, the Alaska State Supreme Court approved both men being on that ballot. This is former President Obama stumped for Democratic candidates in Ohio and Michigan yesterday, sharply criticizing President Trump on his handling of the economy and the war in Iran.
President Trump campaigned in Georgia yesterday and will be in Michigan again today.
And the competitive landscape for this year's midterm elections is stretching deep into places that voted for President Trump in 2024. And Pierre Stephen Bassau or Fowler reports that includes Arkansas, one of the most conservative states in the country.
In the last month, both parties have spent millions of dollars in Arkansas, and Republicans have quintupled their ad spend in the state's second congressional district, according to Ad Impact data.
Democratic nominee Chris Jones says it's because they know affordability concerns have people looking for change.
Folks are literally hurting. And it's to the point where they're saying, "My life is so bad that I don't care about party anymore. I'll look past party in order to change my conditions right now."
The Senate contest between incumbent Republican Tom Cotton and Democrat Hallie Schaffner has flown under the radar compared to many other red state races that have become competitive. But Republicans have spent big there, too, to try and maintain that seat. Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Little Rock, Arkansas.
Voters in Brazil are going to the polls today, and Pierre's carry-con reports it's expected to be the tightest race and presidential in decades.
Brazil's leftist leader, Luisa Nacional de Silva, is facing his toughest political fight as he attempts to force non-consecutive term as president.
Supporters in Brasilia chanted support for the 80-year-old president, who they say is staving off a return to the far right with Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the former president convicted of attempting a coup.
If he wins, the younger Bolsonaro says he'll free his father and restore ties with the U.S. That would add Brazil to the growing list of Latin American countries electing right-wing leaders allied with Trump. Carrie-Con, NPR News, Brasilia.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington. Six Flags says it will add secondary restraints on its rides across the chain that are similar to the roller coaster Goliath at its Georgia Park.
That's where a man died after he was thrown from his seat. Melissa Phato from member station WABE has more.
The seatbelts, similar to those worn in an airplane or car, will be used in addition to the coaster's mechanical restraints, the company says. Some Six Flags rides already use these type of restraints.
CEO John Riley did not specify which attractions will get seatbelts, but eight other rides of the hyper coaster and giga coaster models manufactured by the Swiss firm Bolliger & Mabelard remain closed across the chain.
Goliath also remains closed pending "necessary safety reviews and clearances." Officials are still investigating what caused 42-year-old Hassan Karim's death at Six Flags over Georgia.
This is the first major change the company has announced since the accident earlier this month. For NPR News, I'm Melissa Phato in Atlanta.
Halloween's a week away, but candy sales are off to a slow start as consumers grapple with a high cost of living coupled with eye-watering chocolate prices.
Nielsen IQ market research firm says candy sales fell 6.7 percent in the month ending October 17th compared to the same period last year.
The company says high gas prices have worsened concerns about affordability dampening demand for Halloween treats.
But the National Confectioners Association, which represents candy makers like Mars as the country, is just entering its peak Halloween season.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in Washington.
